Reconnu mondialement pour ses importantes contributions au domaine de l’apprentissage profond, Mila s’est particulièrement distingué dans la modélisation du langage, la traduction automatique, la reconnaissance d’objets et les modèles génératifs. Depuis 2017, Mila est le fruit d’une collaboration entre l’Université de Montréal et l’Université McGill, en lien étroit avec Polytechnique Montréal et HEC Montréal.

 À propos du rôle 
 Le programme FIR est le pari le plus atypique de Mila Ventures : nous réunissons des entrepreneurs expérimentés et certains des meilleurs chercheurs en IA de la planète avec la certitude que des projets extraordinaires en émergeront.  Program Manager, Founders in Residence
 About Mila 
 Founded by Professor Yoshua Bengio of the Université de Montréal, Mila brings together researchers specializing in artificial intelligence, and more specifically in machine learning, deep learning and reinforcement learning. Recognized worldwide for its important contributions to the field of deep learning, Mila has particularly distinguished itself in language modeling, machine translation, object recognition and generative models. Since 2017, Mila has been the fruit of a collaboration between Université de Montréal and McGill University, with close links to Polytechnique Montréal and HEC Montréal.
 Mila's mission is to be a global hub of scientific advances that inspires innovation and the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) for the benefit of all.
 To find out more, please visit https://mila.quebec/ 
 About the role 
 FIR is Mila Ventures' most unusual bet: we take experienced entrepreneurs and put them in a room with some of the best AI researchers on the planet, and we bet that something extraordinary gets built. It usually does — $4M raised so far, real companies formed, real jobs created. Now we need someone to run the room.
 You'll own FIR's marketplace end to end: finding the operators, building trust with the researchers, and making the match happen. You'll be in rooms with CEOs of VC-backed companies as often as you're on campus talking to a postdoc about their thesis. This is a business development role, a recruiting role, and a relationship-management role — most days, all three before lunch.
 What you'll do 
 Identify, recruit and onboard experienced entrepreneurs and operators for the FIR bench — the kind of person a founder would actually want as a co-founder.
 Build real relationships inside the Mila research community, so professors and researchers see FIR as a serious path, not a side project.
 Run the FIR selection committee process end to end, from first conversation to signed match.
 Be a credible, energetic presence with CEOs of VC-backed companies — the one thing everyone on this team needs to be great at.
 Own the numbers: FIR signings, matches made, conversion rate — and fix what isn't working.
 Partner with Program Lead to redesign how we source and qualify talent, and to stand up new initiatives to grow the program (Geographical expansion, Applied AI, Reverse brain-drain).
 What we're looking for 
 Junior-manager level — a few years in, ready to own a program rather than support one.
 A former consultant from a top firm with some exposure to tech or startups is a great fit here — you know how to walk into a room with a CEO and be taken seriously on day one. Not a requirement, but if that's you, we want to talk.
 Genuinely credible with CEOs of VC-backed companies. This is non-negotiable — you'll be doing it constantly.
 High energy, driven, sociable, and mission-driven. If you need to be told to show up excited, this isn't your role.
 Good reasons to work at Mila 
 The opportunity to contribute to a unique mission with a major impact;
 A comprehensive group insurance program (health, dental, disability, life, travel and extended benefits);
 An employee and family assistance program;
 Access to a telemedicine service;
 A vacation policy offering a base of 20 days' vacation upon hiring;
 A retirement savings plan with a minimum employer contribution of 4%;
 A generous flexible package allowing you to tailor your benefits to what contributes to your well-being. You can select and combine options to suit your needs, including lifestyle credits, enhanced insurance, extra vacation days and enriched pension contributions;
 Flexible working hours, a summer schedule and the possibility of telecommuting;
 A work environment in the heart of Little Italy, in the trendy Mile-Ex district, close to public transportation;
 A team of passionate experts in their field;
 A collaborative and inclusive work environment.
 We want to know you 
 At Mila, diversity is important to us. We value a work environment that is fair, open and respectful of differences. We encourage anyone who wants to work in an ecosystem that is constantly evolving and stimulated to contribute to the application and definition of a healthy and inclusive culture, to apply.

We're transforming the grocery industry 
 At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. 
 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.
 Instacart is a Flex First team 
 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. 
 Overview
 Instacart's Enterprise Solutions team partners with Global grocery and retail chains to power their digital commerce through StorefrontPro, Enterprise API (Fulfillment and Ads), CarrotAds, and adjacent Enterprise Solutions products. We're seeking a Director, Customer Success to lead the Customer Success organization — accountable for post-live value realization across the enterprise software portfolio.
 In this highly visible role, you will lead senior managers and Customer Success Managers who serve as the strategic advisor of Instacart to retailer executives. You'll own retailer value realization, measured through adoption velocity, time-to-value, health score coverage, at-risk portfolio management, CSAT, and QBR quality across the portfolio. You'll partner closely with Business Development, who owns NRR, GRR, and expansion, by providing account health, risk signal, and expansion readiness. You'll also partner with Enterprise Solutions Delivery, Technology leadership, and Product on portfolio strategy, retailer signal, and roadmap adoption.
 This is a roll-up-your-sleeves leadership opportunity for someone who has personally led the transformation of CS from reactive enablement toward proactive business advisory, can hire and develop senior consultative talent, and thrives in a fast-paced, BD-led commercial environment with shared standards rather than rigid process. The role reports to the Senior Director, Enterprise Solutions , and is remote across the United States and Canada with a preference for proximity to Toronto for key cross-functional collaboration.
 About the Job
 Lead the Customer Success organization for the Enterprise Solutions portfolio — owning value realization, outcomes end to end, and partner closely with BD, who owns NRR, GRR, and expansion, by providing account health, risk signal, and expansion readiness.Build and develop a senior consultative CS bench by hiring, sponsoring, and ramping Customer Success Managers who engage with retailer executives on ecommerce strategy, merchandising, and operations and who can credibly influence retailer P&L outcomes and roadmap adoption.
 Manage senior managers leading segments, setting standards for what good looks like across the CSM’s — including QBR quality, growth planning, executive engagement, and renewal execution.
 Operate in a BD-led commercial environment as a true commercial peer to BD — preserving BD's ownership of the primary commercial relationship while owning post-sale accountability and surfacing churn, expansion, and escalation signal early and clearly.
 Partner with the Director of Enterprise Architecture & Engineering on shared-account coordination — ensuring the cross-org account team ( CS + Technical Account Managers (TAM’s) ) functions as one team to the retailer despite the functional ownership, with co-authored protocols and clean escalation paths.
 Define and enforce the CSM/TAM boundary based on segmentation — CSM’s lead retailer-executive engagement, value realization, and growth planning, while TAM’s own technical delivery, configuration, and issue resolution, so that CSM capacity stays focused on strategic advisory, not technical execution.
 Own the consultative transformation roadmap — talent strategy, comp structure, operating cadence, and tooling shifts required to evolve CS from a feature-enablement function into a strategic business advisory function.
 Partner with the Director of Retailer Delivery on the implementation-to-success motion as a managed lifecycle (not a document handoff) — ensuring CS is engaged early, named handoff criteria are met, and accounts transition cleanly into early-lifecycle growth ownership.
 Operationalize the retailer segmented model in CS — applying high-touch coverage and scaled/digital-first models, with clear exception protocols and capacity guardrails.
 Build a structured retailer-signal feedback loop into Product — using CS engagements to surface durable patterns (not anecdotes), instrument adoption of roadmap items, and hold CS accountable for adoption outcomes.
 Apply AI augmentation to scale CS coverage and quality without linear headcount growth — including health monitoring, account-prep automation, QBR/insight generation, and signal triage — partnering with the Technical org on tooling roadmap and adoption.
 Represent the post-sale narrative for the portfolio to senior leadership — integrating retention, growth, churn risk, executive-account temperature, and pipeline outlook — and serve as the Director-level escalation point for retailer relationships when CSM-led engagement is insufficient.
 About You
 Minimum Qualifications
 8+ years of enterprise customer success, account management, or post-sale leadership at a B2B SaaS or enterprise technology company.
 Direct, accountable leadership of a customer success organization responsible for adoption velocity, time-to-value, health score, at-risk portfolio, CSAT, QBR quality and support BD with GRR, NRR, and expansion.
 Track record of managing managers with demonstrated ability to set standards and develop senior leaders without micromanagement.
 Ownership of a CS book of business or post-sale P&L of meaningful scale (e.g., $1000M+ ARR) with documented outcomes on Adoption, NRR, GRR, or expansion.
 Proven success operating in a BD- or Sales-led commercial environment — clear instinct for where the CS lane begins and ends, comfort with shared standards rather than rigid RACI/process.
 Demonstrated executive presence with enterprise customer counterparts (VP / SVP / C-level), including the ability to deliver hard news, navigate escalations, and rebuild trust after issues.
 Experience designing and operating segmented CS coverage models (high-touch for strategic accounts, scaled/digital for the long tail), including capacity planning and exception handling.
 Hands-on experience hiring senior CS talent — with a clear point of view on profile, comp, and ramp.
 Strong background having operated in an end to end post sales service delivery ecosystem with strong CS interaction with Business Development/Sales, Delivery, Technical and Product teams. Preferred Qualifications
 Experience transforming a CS function from reactive enablement into proactive business advisory, including the talent, comp, operating-model, and tooling changes required (not a renaming exercise).
 Track record of building or scaling seasoned strategist roles inside a CS org — including hiring profile, ramp, comp design, and integration with the rest of the account team.
 Experience operating with a separate technical TAM function on shared enterprise accounts — including co-authoring cross-org protocols and managing escalations across an org boundary.
 Background applying AI to CS workflows — health monitoring, account preparation, QBR generation, signal triage — with measurable impact on coverage, throughput, or quality.
 Familiarity with the BD/CS interface in commercially complex enterprise sales motions, including renewals, multi-product expansion, and shared-account operating norms.
 Deep familiarity with enterprise retail, grocery, ecommerce platforms, retail media, or adjacent complex B2B domains — including how large retailers evaluate, adopt, and scale technology solutions.
 Experience instrumenting retailer signal into structured product feedback (not anecdotal) and partnering with Product leaders on adoption accountability.

 Leadership and Quality Oversight

About AI Acquisition 
 AI Acquisition is a bootstrapped, founder-led business helping founders and operators scale with AI, combining a sales and delivery engine, one-to-one consultation, and our own SaaS platforms. We move fast, we build constantly, and we hold a high bar for the people who work directly with our clients.
 We currently manage thousands of active clients across multiple products, with 250+ new clients onboarding every month. The Account Management function is the front line of that relationship.
 The Role 
 You are the person between the client and the outcome. Not a relationship manager. Not a check-in scheduler. Not someone who forwards tickets and hopes for the best.
 You own a portfolio of clients who are building real businesses with our support. Some are launching for the first time. Some are scaling. Some are stuck and frustrated. Your job is to diagnose where they actually are, figure out what's blocking their progress, manage their expectations when needed, and drive them toward commercial results, not just activity.
 This means you need to understand marketing, sales, offer development, and fulfillment well enough to have real conversations about all of them. If a client's campaign is generating calls but nobody's closing, you need to be able to tell them why and what to do about it, not pass it to someone else.
 Our clients purchase a fully built AI lead-generation business: brand, website, funnel, lead engine, and the systems that help turn leads into customers. You own the relationship around that delivery. You need to know what they bought, what was promised, where they are in the journey, and what needs to happen next, with specifics, not generalities.
 You'll work directly with clients on Zoom, Slack, and through our internal systems. You'll run growth workshops, intro calls, and quick syncs. You'll manage escalations without panicking and celebrate wins without coasting. And when a client is about to walk, you'll be the person who finds the path to keep them or makes the honest call that they should go.
 What You'll Own: 
 A portfolio of active clients across different stages: onboarding, growth, scale, and at-risk
 Growth workshops, intro calls, and regular check-ins; you set the rhythm, not the client
 Client expectation management, framing what's realistic, resetting when needed, never overpromising
 Diagnosing why a client isn't getting results: is it the offer, the funnel, the sales process, the client's own execution, or something upstream?
 Funnel and campaign literacy and understanding the client's lead engine (Meta ads, cold email, B2B book-a-call, DFY website), confirming it matches their contract and guarantee, and flagging mismatches before they become problems
 Reading the client's specific contract, understanding the distinct payment flows (client pays AIA, client's customers pay client, ad spend reimbursement), and giving accurate answers under pressure rather than quoting generic numbers
 Spotting the signals before a client escalates (sudden silence, short replies, frustration, refund language, contract/funnel mismatches) and acting on them with a structured escalation, not a panicked message
 De-escalating frustrated clients without throwing the company under the bus, without panicking, and without making promises you can't keep
 When you inherit accounts, you verify every client's status, contract, delivery stage, and risk level before assuming anything is fine
 Spotting when a client is ready for more and positioning it as the natural next step, not a sales pitch
 Every client interaction, decision, and next step logged in our systems (Athena ticketing, Slack channels)
 Collaboration with the broader CS, delivery, and onboarding teams to make sure nothing falls through the cracks
 What We Need From You 
 4+ years in a client-facing account management, CSM, or business consulting role where you were directly responsible for client outcomes, not just client satisfaction scores
 You've consulted business owners on how to start, grow, or scale a business, walked them through the hard parts, not just handed them a playbook
 You understand (or can learn fast) the mechanics of B2B lead generation: Meta ads, cold email campaigns, funnels, and how they connect to a client's revenue. You don't need to run campaigns yourself, but you need to diagnose why one isn't converting and have a real conversation about it with the client
 You're comfortable navigating money conversations with clients, not quoting generic numbers, but reading the specific contract, understanding the payment flows, and giving accurate answers under pressure
 You can manage difficult client conversations with composure, you stay calm, you don't blame, you find the path forward
 You come with solutions, not just problems. When something breaks, your instinct is to propose a fix, not report the issue and wait
 You're confident on camera and on calls; clients trust people who sound like they know what they're doing, even under pressure
 You've worked in a startup, agency, or fast-moving environment where things change fast and you had to figure things out without a manual
 You're comfortable with AI tools and either already use them in your workflow or are the kind of person who finds and tests them without being told to
 You don't need to be chased. You manage your own time, your own portfolio, and your own follow-ups
 This Is Not For You If: 
 You only know one side of the equation (only marketing, or only sales) and aren't interested in learning the other
 You need everything documented before you can act; we're building the playbook, not following one
 You wait for clients to come to you with problems instead of spotting them early
 You avoid hard conversations or default to telling clients what they want to hear
 You treat AI as a buzzword rather than something you actually use
 You need heavy management and regular direction to stay productive
 You hear "refund" and freeze instead of diagnosing what went wrong and whether it's fixable
 What Success Looks Like: 
 Your clients are progressing; not just happy, but actually hitting milestones and getting results
 Escalations that reach you don't reach anyone above you, you resolve them
 You're the AM other people point to when asked "who handles clients well here"
 You identify upsell opportunities because you actually understand where the client is and what they need next
 Clients at risk are flagged before they ask for a refund, not after
 You can audit a new book of business end to end and produce an accurate status picture within your first week of owning it
 Your documentation is clean, current, and useful; anyone picking up your account can see exactly where things stand
 You adopt new tools and processes fast and bring ideas for improving them
 Our Process 
 After an initial screen, you'll complete a scenario-based Loom task, a real client situation that tests how you diagnose problems, manage expectations, and make commercial decisions. If you pass, you'll meet with our CS Leadership team for a deeper conversation.
 We assess for judgment, not just experience. Show us how you think.
 The Environment 
 This is a high-performance, remote-first team operating at the cutting edge of AI-powered business building. Here's what that means for you:
 Direct access to founders from day one, no layers, no politics. You'll work alongside people who are building the business, not managing from a distance.
 Real growth path, strong performers are promoted from month three, not year three. We move people up based on what they deliver, not how long they've been here.
 Exposure to AI-led systems and tools, you won't just use AI as a buzzword on your CV. You'll operate inside a business that builds and ships AI products daily, and you'll be expected to use them to get better at your job.
 Compensation that rewards output, base plus performance bonus plus upsell commission. The harder you push, the more you earn.
 Autonomy and ownership, you manage your portfolio, your time, and your client relationships. No micromanagement, no hand-holding.
 A team that holds a high bar, the people around you are operators, not passengers. That's the standard, and it's what makes this place worth being in.
If you're looking for structure handed to you, this isn't the right place. If you want to be the one " Lifting up the hood ", build something real, and raise the bar every week with a team that moves fast - we want to talk.

Les conseiller·ères en acquisition de talents et mobilité interne jouent un rôle essentiel dans la recherche, l'attraction, l'évaluation et la sélection des meilleurs talents externes et internes pour l'organisation. En tant que conseiller·ères en mobilité interne, iels jouent un rôle essentiel en facilitant l'évolution de carrière et les opportunités de développement pour les employés au sein de l'entreprise, en s'appuyant sur leur connaissance approfondie des communautés d'expertise dont iels s'occupent et des besoins spécifiques des projets. 
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Élaborer des stratégies de recrutement et des processus de sélection pour répondre aux besoins de recrutement de tous les studios de la zone.
 Soutenir et guider les gestionnaires pour répondre à leurs besoins en recrutement, en agissant en tant que conseiller de confiance en ce qui concerne la sélection des talents. 
 Accompagner les candidats et les employés tout au long du processus de sélection + documenter les interactions, les suivis et les négociations.
Ce que vous apportez à l’équipe 
 Mapping des talents : Les conseillers en TA&IM doivent avoir une connaissance approfondie du vivier de talents et des compétences de l'organisation afin de pouvoir mettre en adéquation les candidats internes et les postes à pourvoir. Ils doivent être au fait des tendances du secteur, du contexte concurrentiel et de l'évolution de la dynamique du marché des talent afin d'affiner les stratégies de recrutement.
 Évaluation et sélection des candidats : Capacité à évaluer les qualifications, les compétences et l'expérience des candidats afin de déterminer s'ils sont qualifiés pour des postes précis. Ils sont compétents pour créer des processus de sélection structurés, y compris des entretiens efficaces, et pour évaluer les capacités des candidats. 
 Connaissance de l'organisation : Une connaissance approfondie de la structure de l'entreprise, de ses départements, de ses fonctions et de ses rôles est essentielle. Les conseillers doivent être en mesure d'identifier les profils potentiels des candidats par rapport aux postes à pourvoir. Ils doivent fournir des conseils sur la manière dont les employés peuvent progresser et évoluer au sein de l'entreprise en s'appuyant sur des outils et des cadres développés spécifiquement pour la mobilité de carrière. 
 Compétences en négociations : Capacité à négocier la rémunération et les offres d'emploi afin d'obtenir les meilleurs candidats tout en respectant l'équité interne et les critères C&B. De plus, la mobilité interne implique souvent de convaincre les collaborateurs d'accepter un poste prioritaire qui n'est pas forcément celui qu'ils préfèrent. Les conseillers doivent avoir les compétences nécessaires pour négocier des options de recrutement avec les collaborateurs dans de tels scénarios, afin de garantir que les priorités de l'entreprise soient comblées. 
 Gestion de la rétroaction : Fournir une rétroaction constructive aux candidats et aux employés d'une manière professionnelle et constructive, quel que soit le résultat.

The Manager, Model Validation reports to the Director, Model Risk Management and supports the delivery of model validation activities across the Bank. The role executes validation procedures, contributes to validation strategies, and supports the effective management of model risk in accordance with the Bank's Model Risk Management Framework and applicable regulatory requirements. The scope includes models used for credit and treasury risk management, including AIRB and IFRS 9 ECL, interest rate risk, liquidity risk, and stress testing approaches used to support ICAAP.

The role works closely with model risk stakeholders and conducts detailed reviews of model methodologies, assumptions, intended use, limitations, inputs, implementation, and performance. Responsibilities include completing benchmark and outcome analyses, documenting issues and recommendations, drawing evidence-based conclusions, and preparing model validation reports in accordance with the Bank's Model Risk Management Framework (MRMF). The primary focus is the execution of model validation activities, with additional support provided for model governance activities such as regulatory self-assessments, annual attestations, and risk reporting.

Model Validation Projects (85%): Contribute to model validation strategies and maintain model validation plans for assigned reviews.

 Assess modeling data from extraction through preparation, cleansing, and treatment to determine its suitability for model development. Conduct and document model testing, including outcome analysis, sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, stress testing, benchmark analysis, implementation review, and user acceptance testing.
 Prepare clear, well-supported validation reports in accordance with the MRMF. Identify model limitations and weaknesses, define the effective range of model use, and assess model risk in line with MRMF principles.
 Maintain effective communication with model risk stakeholders by setting clear expectations, gathering and sharing required information, and communicating model risk issues and independent recommendations throughout the validation process.
 Support model governance by ensuring model metadata is accurately captured and tracked in the model risk management system. Contribute to annual model attestations, model risk reporting, and other governance activities as required.
Model Risk Management Culture Enablement and Stakeholder Relationship (15%): Maintain current knowledge of industry trends, regulatory expectations, and leading practices in model risk management, and share relevant insights with model risk stakeholders.
 Support stakeholders in understanding and meeting their model risk management responsibilities in accordance with the Bank's MRMF and relevant regulatory guidance.
 Provide independent, constructive feedback to model developers and risk management groups during model development to help identify and remediate model risk issues, while maintaining Model Validation independence.
 Contribute to knowledge sharing across the Model Risk Management team and with relevant stakeholders.
 Develop and maintain productive working relationships with model risk stakeholders across the Bank and provide practical guidance on model risk management matters.
 Escalate difficult, material, or complex project issues to the Director, as appropriate.
 Escalate difficult or complex project-related issues, as appropriate.

 Strong understanding of model risk management and governance.

 An overview of this role 
 As a Staff Renewals Operations Manager at GitLab, you'll help own the operational engine that makes renewals predictable, measurable, and efficient at scale. Reporting to the Director of CX Operations, you'll be the Renewals team's go-to business partner for processes, tooling, forecasting and insights, consumption and subscription data, and the steps required to quote and close a renewal. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. You'll lead through ownership and influence, connecting teams and workflows, turning ambiguous problems into clear next steps, and driving improvements that others across the revenue organization depend on.
 What you'll do 
 Own and continuously improve the end-to-end renewal operating model; from renewal identification, assignment through risk management, quoting, through to close and post-renewal data hygiene processes.
 Develop and improve the operating cadences that guide the renewal business, with a focus on efficiency and process improvement.
 Define, maintain, and evolve retention reporting with cross-functional partners, including gross and net retention, churn and downgrade analysis, and the drivers behind each.
 Partner with Revenue Technology, Revenue Analytics, Finance, and other stakeholders to improve Salesforce and the systems and data flows supporting customer relationship management (CRM), subscription and entitlement records, quoting, orders, billing, and reporting. Translate business needs into requirements, validate solutions, and strengthen data quality and operational controls.
 Simplify and scale the renewal motion through automation, standardized workflows, alerts, playbooks, and self-service insights that reduce manual effort and improve execution consistency.
 Support renewals planning and capacity management, including segmentation implementation, coverage models, productivity assumptions, capacity modeling, supporting target setting, and scenario planning.
 Own and mature the Renewal Operations case-management program, including intake, triage, routing, service-level visibility, resolution, and root-cause analysis. Requests may include user migrations, de-duplication, Renewal Manager ownership changes, compensation exceptions, and Salesforce or data issues.
 Raise the operating standard in your domain by documenting processes, mentoring others on how the renewal motion works, and contributing to broader Revenue Operations initiatives that need the renewals perspective.
 What you'll bring 
 Experience in Renewals Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, management consulting, strategy, or a similar analytical and problem-solving role, with ownership of operational improvements and cross-functional initiatives.
 Hands-on experience with both consumption and subscription renewal motions, including renewal forecasting, retention reporting, and the contractual and process mechanics that govern how renewals close.
 Strong critical thinking and structured problem-solving skills. You can break down ambiguous problems into clear workstreams and move them forward.
 Strong quantitative and analytical skills. You're highly proficient in Excel or Google Sheets, can build and validate models from scratch, and can translate analysis into clear recommendations and action. Experience with Structured Query Language (SQL) or equivalent data-querying tools is preferred, not required.
 Systems thinking and experience using Salesforce for pipeline and renewals reporting. You understand how changes in one part of the go-to-market motion affect others, including how CRM, subscription or entitlement records, quoting, and billing relate to one another, and you design solutions accordingly.
 Sound commercial judgment and an understanding of renewal complexity, including co-terming, amendments, expansions, downgrades, price changes, multiyear agreements, auto-renewals, procurement requirements, and approval policies.
 Strong cross-functional collaboration skills. You build trust with stakeholders at all levels, including field teams and senior leadership, and influence without direct authority.
 Curiosity, sound judgment, and a bias toward action. You learn new domains and tools quickly, move from insight to implementation, and follow through until improvements are adopted and sustained.
 About the team 
 You'll work within CX Operations, partnering closely with Renewals and Customer Success leadership, Sales, Finance, Revenue Technology, and Revenue Analytics. These partnerships connect renewal execution with the processes, systems, and data that support it. In GitLab's all-remote, values-driven environment, documentation, iteration, and cross-functional partnership are core to how you'll work.

Rimkus is a global leader in engineering and technical consulting, providing expert services across the insurance, legal, industrial, and commercial sectors. Our team of engineers, scientists, and technical specialists deliver world-class forensic investigation, failure analysis, and consulting services that support informed decision-making for clients worldwide.
 We are seeking a Senior Structural Engineer with extensive experience in design, construction and failure analysis. This senior-level position will conduct investigations to determine the origin and root causes of failures, structural malfunctions, product defects and performance issues. Complete design of structural restoration and repair works including reconstruction design, repair scope, cost estimates and building permits, following damages due to any cause.
 This role combines technical excellence, investigative expertise, and client-facing consulting to support complex projects involving commercial and industrial facilities and infrastructure. 
 You will have experience working for insurance, legal, industrial and other clients. Skilled at providing oral and written reports of findings and expert testimony.  
 Provide project management and technical oversight of other engineers for multiple projects. Responsible for overseeing the work and managing development of other Engineers and Engineers-in-Training (EITs).

 Practice investigative and interview skills with a broad range of stakeholders to obtain the facts, background and information required to solve complex cases.

 Qualifications

 Experience with large scale complex structural systems in steel, concrete, wood from design concept through construction and final approvals. 
 Prior experience supporting insurance claims, risk assessments and litigation.

Sadie is building technology for hospitality.
 We're looking for an account executive to win new restaurant customers in Vancouver or Calgary, and to run every deal yourself from the first lead to the signed agreement.
 This is a field role. You'll find restaurants through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits, then meet owners in person and show them Sadie working on their own calls. You'll work with onboarding and customer success, so that what you sell goes live well. You'll carry monthly and quarterly targets and own the forecast behind them.
 You decide where to spend your time and which deals to pursue, within agreed pricing and terms. AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research restaurants before a visit, prepare demos, draft proposals and follow-ups, and plan your territory. You're responsible for the quality of everything that goes out under your name.
 What we value
 Sound judgement about which deals are real.
 Taking responsibility for your number and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how a restaurant makes money, and caring whether Sadie improves it.
 Curiosity about why a deal was lost, and a willingness to change your approach.
 The honesty to say a deal is slipping before the forecast says it for you.
 What you'll do
 Win new restaurants, from first visit to signed agreement 
 Most of your time goes on live deals, and most of those deals happen in person. You'll sit down with owners and general managers in their restaurants to learn how the phone is handled today: who answers it, what gets missed during service, and what those missed calls cost in bookings and orders. Then you'll demo Sadie against that picture.
 You'll scope what the restaurant needs, write the proposal, negotiate terms and get the agreement signed. 
 Most of the judgement is in qualification. A good demo with someone who can't sign, or a restaurant Sadie can't serve yet, costs you weeks. You're expected to spot that early and move on.
 Build your own pipeline across your territory 
 You'll generate your own leads through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits. That means planning which neighbourhoods and restaurant groups to work, walking in at the right time of day, and following up until you get a meeting.
 Hit your targets with a forecast you can defend 
 You're measured against monthly and quarterly sales targets, and the expectation is that you hit them consistently. You'll keep every opportunity accurate in HubSpot, so that stage, value and close date mean something to the people who plan around them.
 Represent Sadie where restaurant people meet 
 You'll attend local industry events, restaurant meetups and trade shows across your geography. You'll decide which ones are worth the evening, run the conversations there, and turn them into meetings within the week.
 For a lot of operators, you'll be the first person from Sadie they meet. What they hear from you is what they'll repeat to other owners.
 Hand over accounts that go live well 
 The restaurant buys Sadie, but the guest ringing to book a table decides whether it works. You'll give onboarding and customer success a written record of what you promised, what the owner expects, and what could go wrong.
 If you oversell, the owner finds out on a Friday night and the guest pays for it. Set expectations you can stand behind.
 What you'll bring
 At least 2 years in a closing sales role, selling software or services to businesses in hospitality (ideally full service restaurants) or experience working at full service restaurants.
 A record of meeting targets, and the ability to explain how you did it.
 Experience running the whole cycle yourself, from prospecting through to signature.
 Comfort with in-person selling, including cold visits and demos in front of a busy owner.
 Strong discovery skills. You can find out what an operator needs in fifteen minutes between services.
 Clear written communication. Your proposals and follow-ups are accurate and short.
 An honest forecast. You'd rather call a deal lost than carry it for another month.
 You use AI every day for research, preparation and drafting, and you check what it produces.
 You organise your own week across a territory and follow through without being managed.
 Useful experience
 Selling to restaurants or other hospitality operators.
 Working in a restaurant yourself, front of house or in management.
 Selling reservations, POS, telephony or other restaurant technology.
 An existing network among restaurant owners in your territory.
 Selling AI products to non-technical buyers.
 Being an early sales hire at a startup.
 Who will enjoy this role
 You like finding out how a business really works. When an owner says they miss calls at seven on a Saturday, you want to know how many, what those calls were for, and what happened to the guest who hung up.
 In a single week you might walk into six restaurants before lunch service, run a demo at a bar between shifts, spend an evening at a trade show, and sit with onboarding to sort out an account you signed. Your schedule follows the restaurant day, and some of your best conversations will happen at three in the afternoon or late at night.
